blocks.heading: Specialised Certifications Build Credibility with Recruiters, But

items.text: Google Ads certifications (Search, Display, Measurement)
Free, directly testable in interviews, and covers the platform most performance-marketing entry roles are built around.

blocks.heading: Digital Marketing Roles Suit a Numbers-First Mind

items.text: Not every digital marketing role plays to a commerce background equally, and the order below is not arbitrary: performance marketing leads because it has the clearest route to scaling beyond one employer's pay band, since a track record there converts into freelance or agency work billing multiple clients at once.
Performance marketing / PPC executive
You manage ad spend across Google and Meta, track cost per acquisition, and adjust budgets based on what is converting.

blocks.heading: Use Four Questions for This Decision

items.text: Deciding whether digital marketing is worth building on top of your commerce degree needs more than enthusiasm.
Do you want a numbers-heavy lane (performance marketing, marketing analytics) or a creative-heavy lane (content, social, brand).
Picking the lane that matches your actual coursework preferences beats picking the one that sounds more glamorous online.

blocks.heading: Building Proof with No Agency Job Yet

items.text: Recruiters hiring for entry-level digital marketing roles see the same certificate names on every resume.

A small test campaign on your own page, a friend's small business, or a college fest event page gives you real numbers to talk about in an interview: what the budget was, what the result was, and what you would change next time.
One finished, explainable campaign or dashboard beats five completed certificate courses with nothing built on top of them.

blocks.heading: Mistakes Commerce Students Make Entering Digital Marketing

items.text: Numeric comfort is a real advantage, but recruiters still need to see it applied to an actual campaign, dashboard, or spend decision, not just claimed on a resume.
A stack of free certifications from Google, Meta, and HubSpot looks similar for every applicant.
Even performance-marketing and analytics roles need you to read and give feedback on ad creative and landing pages.
Do not try to decide your entire specialisation this week.
Start with Google Ads and GA4 certifications since they build directly on your existing numeric strength, then build one small practice campaign or dashboard within the same stretch of time.
Run the decision through the four questions above, then pass Three proofs before you commit a longer stretch of learning time to a specific lane.

visuals.heading: Compare the Practical Paths

rows: Reading a P&L or balance sheet
Understanding how marketing spend shows up as a cost line and how conversions eventually show up as revenue, not just "likes."
Basic statistics and percentages
Reading CTR, conversion rate, CPC, and ROAS without needing someone to translate the numbers for you.
Cost and budgeting logic from cost accounting
Allocating an ad budget across channels and defending why a rupee moved from one campaign to another.
Business law and taxation exposure
Understanding GST on ad spend, vendor contracts with agencies, and basic compliance around consumer data and advertising claims.
Comfort with spreadsheets from accounting practicals
Building campaign trackers, pivot tables for spend-vs-result analysis, and basic dashboards without a steep learning curve.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What your degree does not teach you

rows: Platform skill
Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, and Google Analytics 4 are not taught in a BCom syllabus. You need hands-on time inside these tools, not just theory about them.
Content and copy sense
Writing an ad headline or a landing page line is a different skill from writing an exam answer. This needs deliberate practice, not assumption.
SEO and content structure
Keyword research, on-page structure, and basic technical SEO are outside a commerce curriculum entirely and need a separate learning track.
Design literacy
You do not need to become a designer, but reading a Canva or Figma brief and giving useful feedback on a creative is now a baseline marketing skill.
AI-tool fluency
Using AI tools to draft ad variations, analyse campaign data faster, or summarise performance reports is now expected at entry level, not a bonus skill.

blocks.heading: Commerce Vs Mass-Comm Vs Generic BA
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Commerce vs mass-comm vs generic BA: the honest comparison

rows: Commerce (BCom/BBA)
Numeric fluency, budgeting logic, and comfort reading business data feed directly into campaign ROI, spend tracking, and analytics roles.
Needs deliberate work on copywriting, content sense, and design literacy, which commerce coursework does not build.
Mass communication / journalism
Strong head start on copywriting, content structure, and storytelling for brand and social content.
Often weaker on the numbers side: reading a spend report, calculating ROAS, or justifying budget shifts needs separate, deliberate practice.
Generic BA (English, Political Science, etc.)
Can be strong on writing and communication depending on the specific major, with genuine flexibility to specialise either way.
Has the least built-in exposure to either the numbers side or the platform/tool side, so the learning curve on both fronts is usually longer.
